title: Credit Note | Free Word Template
description: Free credit note template: issue a credit to a customer for returns, overcharges or invoice errors.
lead: A document issued by a seller to a buyer crediting the buyer account for returned goods, overcharges, damaged goods, or invoice errors — reducing the amount owed under an existing invoice.
introParagraphs: A credit note (or credit memo) formally records that a customer is owed a credit against an existing invoice. It is issued when goods are returned, an invoice was overcharged, goods were damaged, or a discount needs to be applied after invoicing.

The credit note can be applied against the existing invoice, refunded, or carried forward against future invoices. It keeps your books clean by documenting the reduction without deleting or altering the original invoice.
bullets: Seller and buyer
Your company name, address and tax ID; customer name, address and contact.
Credit note details
Credit note number, date of issue, and reference to the original invoice number/date being credited.
Reason for credit
Brief reason: returned goods, damaged goods, overcharge, discount, pricing error.
Items credited
List each item credited with description, quantity, unit price and amount credited (net of any restocking fee); calculate subtotal, tax and total credit.
Application of credit
How the credit will be applied: refund, applied to outstanding balance, or held against future invoices; payment method if refunded.
howTo: Reference the original invoice
Always tie the credit note to a specific invoice number so accounting is clear.
Itemise the credit
List each product/service credited individually rather than a lump sum; include tax.
State the reason
A short reason (return, damage, discount) keeps records auditable.
Decide on refund vs credit
Confirm with the customer whether they want a refund or a credit on account; process promptly.
Apply in your accounting system
Record the credit note in your books so AR is updated correctly; attach to the original invoice.
related: Issued before an invoice wins the work.
For scope changes that adjust a contract price.
faq: Credit note vs refund?
A credit note is the document; a refund is the action of returning money. Credit notes can also stay on account.
Can I edit the original invoice instead?
No — once issued, invoices should not be altered; credit notes provide a proper audit trail.
Does a credit note include tax?
Yes — reverse the VAT/GST/sales tax that was originally charged on the credited items.
Do I need one for small discounts?
Small goodwill discounts can be done via credit note; for future invoices just issue a new invoice at the lower price.
Is it legally required?
For VAT/GST registered businesses, credit notes are often required to reclaim output tax; best practice everywhere.

title: Purchase Order (PO) | Free Word Template
description: Free purchase order template: formalise orders to suppliers with items, prices, delivery and payment terms.
lead: A buyer-issued document authorising a purchase from a supplier — listing items, quantities, prices, delivery date, shipping address and payment terms; when accepted by the seller it forms a binding contract.
introParagraphs: A purchase order (PO) is issued by a buyer to a vendor to place an order. It lists items, quantities, prices, delivery date, shipping address, payment terms and PO number. When the vendor accepts the PO it becomes a binding contract.
POs create a clear audit trail for both sides, help with inventory/expense tracking, and ensure agreed pricing is in writing before goods are delivered.
bullets: Buyer and vendor
Buyer company, contact, billing and shipping addresses; vendor name, contact and address; PO number and PO date.
Items ordered
SKU/description of each item, quantity, unit price and line total; include tax, shipping and discounts.
Delivery terms
Required delivery date, shipping method/address, Incoterms if international, and any packaging or inspection requirements.
Payment terms
Payment terms (net 30, 50% deposit, COD), accepted payment methods, and any early-payment discount.
Authorisation
Name and signature of the person authorised to approve the purchase; budget/cost centre if applicable.
howTo: Agree pricing first
Confirm quotes/prices with the vendor before issuing the PO — the PO locks in price.
Assign a unique PO number
Use sequential numbering for your records and vendor invoice matching.
List items clearly
SKU, quantity, unit of measure, unit price; reference any vendor quotes by number.
Set delivery expectations
Date, location and FOB/shipping terms; specify who pays shipping and risk of loss.
Send and get acceptance
Email the PO; wait for written acceptance/acknowledgement before expecting shipment.
related: The vendor quote that typically precedes a PO.
If goods are returned/short after a PO/invoice.
Vendor sends an invoice matching the PO to get paid.
faq: Is a PO a binding contract?
Once accepted by the vendor yes; before acceptance it is just an offer to buy.
Do small businesses need POs?
Recommended for anything beyond trivial purchases — they prevent disputes over price, quantity and delivery.
Can I change a PO after it is issued?
With a change order agreed by both sides — issue an amended PO referencing the original number.
PO vs invoice?
PO is buyer to vendor (order); invoice is vendor to buyer (request for payment) referencing the PO number.
What is 2-way vs 3-way matching?
Accounts payable matches invoice to PO (2-way) or invoice + PO + goods receipt (3-way) before paying.

title: Price Quote | Free Word Template
description: Free price quote template: give a customer a fixed price for goods or services with terms and validity period.
lead: A formal document from a seller to a prospective customer stating a fixed price for specified goods or services, with breakdown, terms, and an expiration date (validity period) by which the customer must accept.
introParagraphs: A price quote (or quotation) tells a customer how much you will charge for specific goods or services. It is fixed for a stated period (commonly 30 days) so the customer can accept, after which you provide the goods/service and invoice.
Quotes differ from estimates (which are approximate). Once accepted a quote usually forms the basis of the contract. Itemise clearly so there is no ambiguity about scope.
bullets: Business and customer
Your business name, logo, address and contact; customer name, address and contact; quote number and date.
Scope / items
Description of each line item (goods or services), quantity, unit price, line totals, and any assumptions or inclusions/exclusions.
Pricing totals
Subtotal, discounts, taxes (VAT/GST/sales tax), shipping/expenses if known, and total price.
Terms and validity
How long the quote is valid (e.g. 30 days), payment terms (deposit required, milestones, net terms), delivery timeline, and any exclusions.
Acceptance
Statement that the customer can accept by signing and returning or paying the deposit; space for customer signature/date.
howTo: Understand the scope
Clarify requirements before quoting — misquoted scope kills profit.
Itemise, do not lump
Break out labour, materials, expenses and taxes so the customer sees what they are paying for.
State assumptions
List anything assumed (access, client-provided materials, working hours) so they can be challenged before acceptance.
Set a validity period
Quotes typically expire in 14-30 days to protect you from material-price changes and schedule drift.
Get acceptance in writing
Have the client sign and return (or pay deposit) before starting work; issue an invoice against the accepted quote.
related: Customer PO usually follows an accepted quote.
Invoice against the accepted quote once work is done.
Adjust if something changes after invoicing.
For larger projects a SOW replaces or accompanies the quote.
faq: Quote vs estimate?
A quote is a fixed price the customer can accept; an estimate is an educated guess that may change. Use quotes for well-defined work.
How long should it be valid?
14-30 days is standard; shorter for volatile material prices or time-sensitive offers.
Can I change the price after acceptance?
Only via a change order agreed in writing; otherwise the accepted price is the contract price.
Should I include tax?
Yes — show net, tax and gross so the customer knows the total; customers hate surprise tax.
Is a verbal quote binding?
Harder to prove — always put quotes in writing to avoid disputes.

title: Payment Receipt | Free Word Template
description: Free payment receipt: acknowledge payment received for goods or services with date, amount and method.
lead: A written acknowledgment that a payment has been received — showing date, amount, payment method, what it was for, and who received it.
introParagraphs: A payment receipt proves someone paid you. Issue one every time you receive payment (especially for cash or in-person transactions) and give a copy to the payer; keep one for your records.

Receipts are important for customer confidence, tax records, and resolving disputes about whether something was paid. They are simpler and more general than a rent receipt or invoice — they confirm payment, not the underlying obligation.
bullets: Payer and recipient
Your name/business and contact; payer name; date and receipt number.
Payment details
Amount paid (in numbers and words), payment method (cash, cheque, card, transfer, crypto), and cheque/transaction ID.
What it was for
Description of what the payment covers (invoice #, service, goods, deposit, rent period), and any remaining balance.
Paid in full / partial
Whether the payment settles the full amount or is a partial payment (and the outstanding balance).
Signature
Recipient signature/initials and date; business stamp if used.
howTo: Issue at time of payment
Give the receipt when you receive the funds — do not backdate.
Use a sequential number
Number receipts for accounting and lookup.
State the payee and purpose
Who paid and what for (invoice number, goods, deposit) prevents confusion later.
Note partial payments
If paying in instalments, show the total, amount paid and remaining balance.
Keep a copy
Paper: use a duplicate/receipt book; digital: save a PDF or printed copy for your records.
related: Rent-specific receipt with property and period.
Send before payment is made; receipt confirms it landed.
Invoice and receipt templates in multiple formats.
faq: Is a receipt required by law?
In many places you must give a receipt for cash payments on request; it is best practice for all payments.
Email or paper?
Either works as long as it shows the required details; digital receipts are easier to track.
Do receipts need tax?
If you are collecting sales tax/VAT, show the tax component; if it is a private sale, a plain receipt is fine.
Is a bank transfer confirmation enough?
It shows funds moved but not what they were for — issue a proper receipt referencing the invoice/purpose.
Do I need one for every small payment?
For any cash payment yes; for card/online, the system receipt plus an invoice is usually enough.

title: Job Description | Free Word Template
description: Free job description: define a role duties, requirements, reporting line, compensation range and benefits.
lead: A document describing a role being hired for — title, department, reporting line, responsibilities, required/desired qualifications, location, compensation range and benefits.
introParagraphs: A job description (JD) defines a role for hiring, performance management and legal compliance. It tells candidates what the job entails, sets expectations for employees, and supports pay equity by describing role levels consistently.

Keep job descriptions current — update when duties change. Avoid language that could discourage protected groups (e.g. 'rockstar', 'energetic recent grad') and list essential vs marginal functions to support ADA accommodation decisions.
bullets: Role basics
Job title, department, reports-to, location (on-site/hybrid/remote), employment type (full-time/part-time/contract) and FLSA status (exempt/non-exempt).
Role summary
A 2-3 sentence overview of why the role exists and its primary purpose.
Key responsibilities
5-10 bullet points of core duties and outcomes (start with verbs, focus on results).
Requirements
Required qualifications (education, years of experience, skills, certifications) and preferred qualifications — separate must-haves from nice-to-haves.
Compensation and benefits
Salary range (required by pay-transparency laws in many US states), bonus/equity, benefits, and equal-opportunity employer statement.
howTo: Start with outcomes
Define what success in the role looks like in 6-12 months, not just a task list.
Be specific about skills
List concrete technical/soft skills rather than vague traits (e.g. 'proficient with SQL' vs 'data driven').
Include pay range
Pay-transparency laws in CA, NY, CO, WA and others require a salary range — always include one.
Separate essential functions
Identify duties fundamental to the role to support ADA accommodation decisions.
Review before posting
Have hiring manager and HR/legal review; update with each hiring round to reflect the role accurately.
related: Sent after a candidate accepts the role.
Used when an employee is not meeting JD expectations.
faq: Is a job description a contract?
No — it describes the role but most US employment is at-will; duties can evolve.
Do I have to post the salary range?
Required by law in many US states (CA, CO, NY, WA, and others) and growing — best practice always.
How long should it be?
1-2 pages is ideal; long lists of duties discourage candidates.
Can I require a degree?
Only if it is genuinely necessary — degree inflation discourages diverse candidates and may have legal implications.
Should I list every duty?
Cover the major responsibilities; add 'other duties as assigned' so the role can evolve.
